behavior.arguments: rdi = out pointer; rsi = 32-byte subtrahend pointer; rdx = 32-byte minuend pointer (modified in place)
behavior.borrow_trick: after the word-2 sbb, setb captures the low-word borrow in al; add $0xff,%al turns al=1 into CF=1 (and al=0 into CF=0), so sbb $0x0,%r9 subtracts exactly the borrow-in from the top word; setb then captures the overall borrow-out in cl

edges.covered_borrow: minuend top=1, low=0 minus subtrahend 1: flag 1, out = 2^192-1 (low borrow covered by top word)
edges.equal_top_low_borrow: minuend top=1, low=0 minus subtrahend top=1, low=1: flag 0, out untouched, minuend rewritten to all 0xff
edges.zero_minus_one: flag 0, out untouched, minuend rewritten to all 0xff

behavior.minuend_side_effect: the minuend at rdx is rewritten with the raw 32-byte difference in BOTH cases: words 0-2 by the sub/sbb chain, word 3 stored at 0x2760a42 before the borrow checks; only the copy to out+8 and the flag value 1 are success-gated
behavior.output_shape: 8-byte flag at (rdi) plus, on success only, 32-byte difference at (rdi)+8; no other return value
behavior.subtract_rule: out_flag = 1 if minuend >= subtrahend as 256-bit unsigned, else 0; on success out+8 = minuend - subtrahend (32 bytes, little-endian)

caller_fde.note: all three sites confirmed as instruction starts by linear disassembly from the caller FDE start; the .text byte-pattern scan is not a complete xref census

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, no runtime rebase
